Deploys the connector tile, ASIM parser, two analytics rules, two hunting queries, a workbook, and three SOAR playbooks (as nested deployments), and registers the solution package. Validate with the Sentinel solution packaging tool before Content Hub submission.
metadata.description: One Azure deployment that creates the Data Collection Endpoint, Data Collection Rule and tables that Abstract Security sends events to through the Logs Ingestion API, and installs Microsoft Sentinel content for that data.
Log Analytics / Sentinel workspace name.
Custom table the Abstract Sentinel Destination writes to.
Connector tile logo. Defaults to the embedded Abstract Security mark (self-contained data URI).
Abstract API base URL (used by the playbooks).
Abstract vendor account id for the playbooks (x-as-vendor-account-id). Leave blank to configure later.

Key Vault secret URI for the Abstract API key, with ?api-version, for example https://<vault>.vault.azure.net/secrets/abstract-api-key?api-version=7.4. Used only when keyVaultMode is None, the default: playbooks fetch it at runtime through their managed identity (grant each 'Key Vault Secrets User'). With keyVaultMode Create or Existing the template points the playbooks at the secret it stored. The key is never stored in the template. Leave empty to install the playbooks without it; they fail until it is set.
Enrich-incident playbook lookback window (hours).

Where this deployment stores the Abstract API key the playbooks call Abstract with. None, the default, stores nothing: the playbooks read the secret keyVaultSecretUri names, and you grant their roles yourself. Create makes a Key Vault in this resource group, in its region, (RBAC authorization, soft delete with 7-day retention, purge protection on, public network access enabled, no network rules) and writes abstractApiKey into it. A rerun with Create applies those settings to the vault again, so a vault you locked down afterwards (firewall, private endpoint) is opened again: once the vault exists, rerun with Existing. Existing writes abstractApiKey into the vault keyVaultName names, which must be in this resource group and use RBAC authorization for the role grants to apply. With Create or Existing, keyVaultSecretUri is ignored. Find existing vaults: Azure portal > Key vaults, filtered to this resource group. Default: None. Example: Create.

The Abstract API key, written as a Key Vault secret when keyVaultMode is Create or Existing, and required then. A secure parameter: it never appears in the deployment's inputs, outputs or history. A rerun with Create or Existing needs the key again and writes it as a new version of the secret. Find it: the API key Abstract issued for your tenant, or ask Abstract. Default: empty.

Name of the Key Vault. Create: 3 to 24 letters, digits and hyphens, unique in Azure; empty generates abskvs-<hash> from this resource group and keyVaultNameSuffix. Existing: the exact name of a vault in this resource group. Used only when keyVaultMode is Create or Existing. Purge protection keeps a deleted vault's name reserved for its 7-day retention. Find it: Azure portal > Key vaults > Name. Default: empty. Example: abstract-sentinel-kv.

Text mixed into the generated Key Vault name (keyVaultMode Create with keyVaultName empty), so a redeploy gets a new name. Set it after you deleted the resource group or the vault: purge protection keeps the deleted vault, and its name, for 7 days, and the same generated name then fails with VaultAlreadyExists. Empty, the default, keeps the name earlier runs generated. Find deleted vaults: Azure portal > Key vaults > Manage deleted vaults. Default: empty. Example: 2.

Name of the secret that holds the Abstract API key, 1 to 127 letters, digits and hyphens. Used only when keyVaultMode is Create or Existing; a secret of that name already in the vault gets a new version. Find it: Key vaults > the vault > Objects > Secrets. Default: abstract-api-key. Example: abstract-api-key.

Grant each playbook's managed identity Key Vault Secrets User on the stored secret (the secret only, not the vault) and Microsoft Sentinel Responder on the workspace, the two roles the playbooks need to run. Applies only when this deployment stores the key (keyVaultMode Create or Existing); with keyVaultMode None nothing is granted. Needs Owner, or User Access Administrator, on this resource group. Find the grants: Key vaults > the vault > Objects > Secrets > the secret > Access control (IAM), and the workspace > Access control (IAM). It is the master switch: grantPlaybookResponder and grantPlaybookSecretsUser leave out one role each, for playbooks that already hold it. Default: true. Example: true.

With grantPlaybookRoles, grant Microsoft Sentinel Responder on the workspace to each playbook. Turn it off when the playbooks already hold that role from an assignment made outside this deployment: Azure refuses a second assignment of the same role to the same identity on the same scope (RoleAssignmentExists), which fails the deployment. It applies to all three playbooks, so if only some hold the role, grant it to the others yourself and turn this off. Find the grants: the workspace > Access control (IAM) > Role assignments. Default: true. Example: false.

With grantPlaybookRoles, grant Key Vault Secrets User on the stored secret to each playbook. Turn it off when the playbooks already hold that role on the secret from an assignment made outside this deployment, which would otherwise fail with RoleAssignmentExists. It applies to all three playbooks, so if only some hold the role, grant it to the others yourself and turn this off. Find the grants: Key vaults > the vault > Objects > Secrets > the secret > Access control (IAM). Default: true. Example: false.

properties.displayName: Abstract Security - High or Critical event
properties.description: High/critical Abstract event; surfaces AbstractInsightId for the Verdict playbook.
properties.query:
AbstractEventLogs_CL
| extend AbstractEvent = iff(isnotnull(column_ifexists('AbstractEvent', dynamic(null))), column_ifexists('AbstractEvent', dynamic(null)), pack_all()), Message = tostring(column_ifexists('Message', ''))
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| extend e = AbstractEvent
| extend AbstractSeverity=tolower(tostring(e.severity)), SrcIpAddr=coalesce(tostring(e.source_ipv4),tostring(e.source_address)), ActorUsername=coalesce(tostring(e.user_name),tostring(e.user_id)), AbstractInsightId=coalesce(tostring(e.id), tostring(e.acs_id)), EventProduct=tostring(e.product), EventMessage=coalesce(tostring(e.message),Message)
| where AbstractSeverity in ("high","critical")
| project TimeGenerated, AbstractSeverity, EventProduct, EventMessage, SrcIpAddr, ActorUsername, AbstractInsightId

properties.displayName: Abstract - Repeated auth failures followed by success
properties.description: Detects a likely successful brute force / password spray: many failed authentication events followed by a success from the same source IP within a short window, using Abstract-normalized auth telemetry (ASim_AbstractEvent). Tune the EventResult terms to your products.
properties.query:
let failures = ASim_AbstractEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
  | where EventType has_any ("auth", "login", "logon") or EventResult has "fail"
  | where EventResult has_any ("fail", "failure", "denied")
  | summarize Failures = count(), FailUsers = make_set(ActorUsername, 25) by SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
  | where Failures >= 10;
let successes = ASim_AbstractEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
  | where EventResult has_any ("success", "succeeded", "allowed")
  | project SuccessTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, ActorUsername, AbstractInsightId = AbstractEventId, EventProduct;
failures
| join kind=inner successes on SrcIpAddr
| where SuccessTime between (TimeGenerated .. (TimeGenerated + 10m))
| where set_has_element(FailUsers, ActorUsername)
| project SuccessTime, SrcIpAddr, ActorUsername, Failures, EventProduct, AbstractInsightId
| sort by Failures desc

properties.displayName: Abstract - Rare or newly-seen product activity
properties.query:
ASim_AbstractEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| summarize Events = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by EventProduct, EventVendor
| where Events < 50 and FirstSeen > ago(3d)
| extend Rarity = round(1.0 / Events, 4)
| sort by Events asc

tags.value: Surfaces products/sources in the Abstract pipeline that are rare or first seen in the last few days (shadow IT, misconfigured route, or attacker enabling a new logging surface).

properties.query:
ASim_AbstractEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d) and isnotempty(AbstractIdentity)
| summarize TotalRisk = sum(EventRiskScore), Events = count(), Products = make_set(EventProduct, 10), SrcIps = make_set(SrcIpAddr, 10), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by AbstractIdentity, ActorUsername
| where TotalRisk > 100 and array_length(Products) >= 2
| sort by TotalRisk desc
